title: Rimini Street Launches Rimini Govern™ for AI to Deliver Comprehensive AI Agent Governance, Security & Interoperability as a Service
summary: The new service enables organizations to implement & operationalize an enterprise-wide AI agent governance, security & performance measurement solution.
body_text: The new service enables organizations to quickly and easily implement and operationalize a global, enterprise-wide governance, control, security and performance measurement solution for AI agent activity and workflows LAS VEGAS – July 30, 2026 – Rimini Street, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMNI), the Software Support and Agentic AI ERP Company™ and the leading third-party support provider for Oracle, SAP and VMware software, today announced the immediate availability of Rimini Govern™ for AI, the newest offering in the company’s Rimini Govern portfolio of Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) solutions. The new managed service is delivered 24/7/365 through Rimini Street’s Global Command Centers by expert AI engineers to help organizations: Accelerate AI agent deployment Reduce AI agent operational risk Increase visibility into AI agent activity Provide AI agent activity audit capability Control AI agent operating costs Measure business value from AI agent investments Scale AI agent adoption confidently Rimini Govern for AI provides a centralized operational control plane for AI agents, assisting organizations with overall management by: Monitoring agent activity, workflows, security events, compliance status, performance metrics and cost data across the enterprise Ensuring agents only perform authorized activities and successfully complete approved workflows Enforcing security, governance and compliance guardrails Measuring Agentic AI ROI and business value Enabling rapid intervention by Rimini Street’s expert AI engineers when necessary The service also includes root-cause analysis and remediation support to resolve AI agent issues quickly, minimize operational disruption, and maintain stability across AI-enabled workflows and business processes. “With Rimini Govern for AI, organizations can now confidently and securely deploy AI agents and scale AI agent operations with the oversight, control, visibility and measurement needed to accelerate adoption, measure ROI and achieve business outcomes that include reduced total operating costs, improved profitability and enhanced competitive advantage,” said Seth Ravin, CEO, Rimini Street. “With more than twenty years of proven experience delivering global, ultra-responsive, mission-critical IT support to thousands of organizations around the world — including public sector, critical infrastructure and military clients with security-clearance requirements — Rimini Street is uniquely positioned to deliver industry-leading capabilities in global AI agent governance, security, compliance and interoperability.” “As organizations move from AI experimentation to enterprise-scale adoption, they need trusted visibility, governance and control to deploy AI responsibly and securely,” said R “Ray” Wang, CEO, Constellation Research. “Customers want AI solutions to provide a centralized foundation for enterprises to secure, run, govern and measure AI effectiveness at scale. When you combine this with proven enterprise software support and deep process knowledge, global managed service capabilities 24/7/365 from Global Command Centers and expansive AI expertise, organizations can now operationalize AI with speed, cost-effectiveness and confidence. This is a no-brainer.” A Growing AI Agent Control Gap As organizations accelerate Agentic AI adoption, many lack reliable visibility into AI agent and workflow operational execution, security management and integrations. Many are also struggling with “shadow AI,” including fragmented monitoring tools, inconsistent governance frameworks across business units and the inability to measure AI agent performance, cost and ROI at enterprise scale. The result is a growing “control gap” between AI agent opportunities and required operational management across various enterprise software, platforms and systems. In fact, “Gartner® predicts that by 2027, 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous AI agents due to governance gaps identified only after production incidents occur.”1 An Operating and Management Model for Enterprise AI Rimini Govern for AI closes the enterprise AI control gap with a new managed operating solution for Agentic AI. The service brings together AI governance capabilities, deep enterprise application expertise, and global managed services that enable organizations to control, secure and scale AI agent activity with confidence. The Rimini Govern for AI subscription service is a quick, easy, three-phase deployment and can be fully operational in just weeks: Plan: Rimini Street AI agent experts assess a client’s AI agent goals, current-state readiness, governance priorities and roadmap needs, providing key recommended actions through complimentary Rimini AI Readiness Assessment and Rimini AI Strategy and Roadmap workshops led by a Rimini Street Enterprise Architect. Implement: Rimini Street works with clients to implement Rimini Govern for AI and to (a) discover all agents across the designated software, platforms and systems; (b) configure secure access needed to govern AI agent activity and workflows; and (c) assess the operational, financial and compliance impact of AI agents and workflows. Operate: Real-time, 24/7/365 delivery of the Rimini Govern for AI service is provided by expert Rimini Street AI engineers located in Rimini Street’s Global Command Centers, which also have integrated 24/7/365 system monitoring, security and integration as a service staff. End-to-End Agentic AI Solutions Rimini Govern for AI is part of the growing Rimini Govern™ suite of governance, risk and compliance services from Rimini Street, supporting mission-critical enterprise software and system operations for thousands of organizations around the world — including Global 100, Fortune 500, public sector and military clients. Built on a proven, unified delivery model developed over more than 20 years of supporting mission-critical enterprise software from SAP, Oracle, VMware, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow and many other software vendors, the service is especially suited for organizations — including those in highly regulated or security-cleared operations — that want to securely deploy AI agents into production leveraging various AI tools, platforms or vendors and are seeking to measure ROI from AI investments. Together, Rimini Agentworks™, Rimini Agentic UX™ and Rimini Govern™ for AI provide organizations with an end-to-end set of services to design, deploy, govern and optimize AI agent operations across mission-critical enterprise environments. Rimini Agentworks is a comprehensive AI agent lifecycle service that enables organizations to move from AI concepts to trusted production deployment. The service helps clients define agent strategies, design and build AI agents and workflows, validate interoperability, perform functional and security testing, and certify operational readiness. As part of this process, Rimini Agentworks helps ensure — before any approved deployment — that AI agents operate within approved business, accuracy, security and compliance guardrails and meet stringent requirements for governance, monitoring and production operation. Rimini Agentworks tests and certifies both AI agents developed by Rimini Street and those from other third parties. Rimini Agentic UX is an intelligent, AI-driven user engagement layer deployed over the top of existing ERP systems and releases, enabling a modern user, role and persona-based experience and automating workflows that leverage AI agents. With Rimini Agentic UX Solutions, organizations can connect data, unearth insights and make decisions based on recommended actions that optimize ERP Processes and drive immediate productivity enhancements across the organization for greater competitive advantage. For more information about the Rimini Street portfolio of governance, risk and compliance solutions that include Rimini Govern for AI, or to schedule a complimentary AI strategic assessment or roadmapping workshop, please visit the Rimini Govern for AI web page . 1Source: Gartner Press Release, Gartner Says Applying Uniform Governance Across AI Agents Will Lead to Enterprise AI Agent Failure , May 2026. Gartner is a trademark of Gartner, Inc. and/or its affiliates.

title: Panduan Kerja Barista di Turki: Syarat, Gaji, dan Dana Talangan Danacita
summary: Panduan lengkap kerja barista di Turki, mulai dari syarat, kisaran gaji, biaya hidup, peluang kerja, hingga solusi dana talangan Danacita untuk membantu proses keberangkatan.
body_text: Daftar isi Panduan Kerja Barista di Turki: Syarat, Gaji, dan Dana Talangan Danacita Industri kopi di Turki terus berkembang seiring meningkatnya jumlah kedai kopi lokal maupun internasional. Tidak hanya terkenal dengan kopi khas Turki yang telah diakui UNESCO sebagai warisan budaya dunia, negara ini juga memiliki banyak kafe modern yang membutuhkan tenaga kerja di bidang food and beverage (F&B), termasuk barista. Bagi masyarakat Indonesia yang memiliki pengalaman meracik kopi atau bekerja di coffee shop, peluang untuk bekerja sebagai barista di Turki cukup menarik. Selain memperoleh pengalaman internasional, pekerjaan ini juga dapat menjadi batu loncatan untuk mengembangkan karier di industri hospitality. Sebelum memutuskan berangkat, penting untuk memahami syarat kerja, kisaran gaji, biaya yang perlu dipersiapkan, hingga solusi pembiayaan apabila dana keberangkatan belum mencukupi. Mengapa Kerja Barista di Turki Menarik? Turki merupakan salah satu destinasi yang cukup diminati pekerja asing karena memiliki sektor pariwisata yang berkembang. Banyak hotel, restoran, dan coffee shop melayani wisatawan dari berbagai negara setiap harinya. Beberapa alasan profesi barista di Turki menarik antara lain: Kesempatan memperoleh pengalaman kerja internasional. Budaya kopi yang sangat kuat sehingga kemampuan barista terus berkembang. Peluang meningkatkan kemampuan bahasa Inggris maupun bahasa Turki. Berkesempatan bekerja di jaringan coffee shop internasional. Pengalaman kerja luar negeri dapat meningkatkan nilai CV untuk jenjang karier berikutnya. Syarat Kerja Barista di Turki Persyaratan dapat berbeda pada setiap perusahaan atau pemberi kerja. Namun secara umum, berikut beberapa syarat yang biasanya diminta. 1. Berusia Produktif Mayoritas perusahaan mencari kandidat berusia sekitar 20–35 tahun , meskipun batas usia dapat berbeda tergantung kebutuhan perusahaan. 2. Memiliki Pengalaman Sebagai Barista Pengalaman bekerja di coffee shop menjadi nilai tambah. Umumnya perusahaan lebih menyukai kandidat yang memiliki pengalaman minimal 1–2 tahun . 3. Menguasai Teknik Dasar Barista Kemampuan yang biasanya dibutuhkan meliputi: Mengoperasikan mesin espresso. Membuat berbagai jenis minuman kopi. Latte art dasar. Menjaga kebersihan area kerja. Memberikan pelayanan yang baik kepada pelanggan. 4. Mampu Berkomunikasi Kemampuan bahasa Inggris biasanya menjadi syarat utama, terutama apabila bekerja di kota besar seperti Istanbul atau Antalya. Beberapa perusahaan juga memberikan nilai tambah bagi kandidat yang memiliki kemampuan dasar bahasa Turki. 5. Memiliki Dokumen yang Lengkap Dokumen yang biasanya diperlukan antara lain: Paspor yang masih berlaku. Visa kerja. Work permit dari perusahaan di Turki. Surat kesehatan apabila diminta. Dokumen pendukung lainnya sesuai ketentuan perusahaan. Berapa Gaji Barista di Turki? Besaran gaji bergantung pada lokasi kerja, pengalaman, jenis coffee shop, serta jam kerja. Secara umum, kisaran gaji barista di Turki berada di angka: 30.000–45.000 Lira Turki (TRY) per bulan Apabila menggunakan estimasi kurs sekitar Rp420 per 1 TRY , maka penghasilannya setara dengan: Sekitar Rp12,6 juta–Rp18,9 juta per bulan Di beberapa perusahaan, pekerja juga berpotensi memperoleh tambahan berupa: Tip dari pelanggan. Bonus kinerja. Makan selama bekerja. Tempat tinggal (untuk beberapa lowongan tertentu). Asuransi kesehatan sesuai kebijakan perusahaan. Besaran fasilitas tersebut berbeda-beda tergantung pemberi kerja. Estimasi Biaya Berangkat Kerja ke Turki Sebelum mulai bekerja, terdapat beberapa biaya yang biasanya perlu dipersiapkan. Nominalnya dapat berbeda tergantung jalur perekrutan dan kebijakan perusahaan. Berikut gambaran estimasi biaya yang umum diperlukan. Kebutuhan Estimasi Biaya None Pembuatan paspor Rp350.000–Rp650.000 None Medical check-up Rp500.000–Rp2.000.000 None Pengurusan dokumen Rp1.000.000–Rp5.000.000 None Tiket pesawat Indonesia–Turki Rp8.000.000–Rp18.000.000 None Dana kebutuhan awal Rp5.000.000–Rp15.000.000 None Secara keseluruhan, kebutuhan dana keberangkatan biasanya berada di kisaran Rp15 juta hingga Rp40 juta , tergantung apakah perusahaan menanggung sebagian biaya atau seluruh biaya ditanggung oleh calon pekerja. Peluang Karier Setelah Menjadi Barista Profesi barista tidak hanya sebatas membuat kopi. Dengan pengalaman yang cukup, jenjang karier dapat berkembang menjadi: Senior Barista. Head Barista. Coffee Trainer. Supervisor Coffee Shop. Store Manager. Quality Control Beverage. Konsultan atau Trainer Kopi. Pengalaman bekerja di luar negeri juga dapat menjadi nilai tambah apabila ingin melanjutkan karier di hotel berbintang, restoran internasional, atau membuka usaha coffee shop sendiri di Indonesia. Tips Agar Mudah Diterima Kerja Sebagai Barista di Turki Persaingan kerja tentu tetap ada. Agar peluang diterima semakin besar, beberapa hal berikut dapat dipersiapkan sejak awal. Perbanyak pengalaman bekerja di coffee shop. Pelajari dasar bahasa Inggris dan bahasa Turki. Ikuti pelatihan atau sertifikasi barista. Siapkan CV berbahasa Inggris. Latih kemampuan customer service. Lamar melalui perusahaan atau agen penyalur tenaga kerja yang resmi dan memiliki izin. Dana Talangan Danacita untuk Persiapan Kerja ke Turki Persiapan bekerja di luar negeri sering kali membutuhkan dana yang tidak sedikit. Mulai dari pengurusan dokumen, pemeriksaan kesehatan, tiket pesawat, hingga kebutuhan hidup pada masa awal keberangkatan. Apabila dana yang tersedia belum mencukupi, Dana Talangan Danacita dapat menjadi salah satu solusi pembiayaan untuk membantu memenuhi kebutuhan biaya persiapan tersebut. Dengan skema pembiayaan yang disesuaikan dengan ketentuan yang berlaku, calon pekerja dapat lebih fokus mempersiapkan proses keberangkatan tanpa harus menunda peluang kerja yang sudah diperoleh. Sebelum mengajukan pembiayaan, pastikan memahami seluruh syarat, ketentuan, biaya, serta kemampuan membayar cicilan agar kondisi keuangan tetap terjaga.

(NASDAQ: PRPO) , will be hosting its Q2-2026 shareholder update call on August 17th, 2026, at 5:00 PM ET. The conference call may be accessed by calling 646.307.1865. All callers should ask for the Precipio Inc. conference call. A replay of the call will be available approximately 24 hours after the call and may be accessed via the Investors page on Precipio’s website, https://www.precipiodx.com/investors/ . About Precipio Precipio is a healthcare biotechnology company focused on cancer diagnostics. Our mission is to address the pervasive problem of cancer misdiagnoses by developing solutions in the form of diagnostic products and services. Our products and services deliver higher accuracy, improved laboratory workflow, and ultimately better patient outcomes, which reduce healthcare expenses. Precipio develops innovative technologies in our laboratory where we design, test, validate, and use these products clinically, improving diagnostic outcomes. Precipio then commercializes these technologies as proprietary products that serve the global laboratory community and further scales Precipio’s reach to eradicate misdiagnosis. title: Top DesignJoy Alternatives to Try in 2026
summary: Compare the best DesignJoy alternatives for 2026, with real pricing, pros and cons, and how to pick a design service that scales past one solo designer.
body_text: Key takeaways: DesignJoy runs on a single $4,995/month plan handled by one person, so you're paying a premium rate with no team behind it and one request moving at a time. The best alternatives give you a team instead of a solo operator, a lower entry price, or the ability to run several projects at once. Awesomic matches you with vetted talent in up to 24 hours and covers design, no-code, and video under one fee, with a dedicated project manager available on higher tiers. Match the alternative to your real need: parallel throughput, a named team, bundled video, or a budget-friendly entry point all point to different picks. DesignJoy built its reputation on a simple promise: one senior designer, a flat monthly fee, and fast turnaround. For a founder who wants a single skilled hand on brand and web work, that model still appeals. But it comes with real trade-offs. At $4,995/month for a single plan run by one operator, you're betting on one person's availability, working one request at a time, with no lower tier to grow into. This guide covers the best DesignJoy alternatives worth trying in 2026, what each does well, real pricing, and how to choose. We build one of them, Awesomic, so we'll be clear about where we fit and where another option is the better call. Every other service is described on the facts. Why look for DesignJoy alternatives? DesignJoy does one thing well, so the reasons to look elsewhere tend to be about scale, price, and risk rather than quality. The most common ones: One person handles everything, so capacity is capped and there's no team backup if that person is unavailable. Work moves one request at a time, which slows any team that needs several projects running in parallel. There's a single plan at $4,995/month with no cheaper tier, so you can't start small and scale up. The account is capped at two users, which is tight for a growing marketing team. The solo-operator risk isn't hypothetical. In a Reddit AMA, DesignJoy's founder confirmed the whole service runs through him, and that the realistic worst case if he's unavailable is pausing all subscriptions until he's back ( shared on Reddit , so weigh it as one founder's own words). That's the honest limitation team-based services are built to avoid, and it's worth reading our founder's guide to hiring designers before you decide how to staff design at all. None of this makes DesignJoy a poor choice for the right buyer. It means teams that need parallel throughput, a lower entry price, or team redundancy have strong reasons to compare. That shift toward flexible, on-demand creative is widespread: Upwork's Future Workforce Index found 38% of U.S. skilled knowledge workers are freelancing in 2026, up from 28% a year earlier. The best DesignJoy alternatives Here's how the top alternatives compare. Awesomic leads the table as the option we build, with its pricing and limits stated plainly so you can judge the fit. Pricing is the lowest public monthly rate for a comparable plan; ratings reflect our read of value, breadth, and reliability. Service Best for Key strengths Main limitation Pricing (from) Rating Awesomic Startups needing design, web, and video Vetted talent matched in 24h, broad scope, dedicated PM option Not the cheapest entry point $1,490/month ★★★★★ Design Pickle Managed graphics at scale Brand-trained team, fast first drafts Quote-only, no public pricing Custom ★★★★½ Penji Simple marketing graphics on a budget Low $499 entry, art-director oversight 1 project at a time on entry tier $499/month ★★★★½ Kimp Bundled graphics and video Graphics + video in one fee, dedicated team 2–5 active requests by plan $1,397/month ★★★★ ManyPixels Startups wanting source files and IP Full IP transfer, choose your designer No sub-$500 or free tier $699/month ★★★★ Superside Enterprise creative at scale Senior AI-native teams, huge breadth $15,000/month floor, annual term $15,000/month ★★★★ Flocksy One dedicated creative team Same team every brief, rollover hours Best rates need annual billing $1,199/month ★★★★ Delesign A named designer at a mid-tier price Dedicated senior designer, keep work on refund Queue is ~2 hours/day, serial $599/month ★★★★ Kapa99 Fast, flat-fee parallel design Unlimited parallel tasks, free trial Output can be uneven $499/month ★★★½ DotYeti Clear turnaround SLAs Published day-based SLAs, 3D on top tiers Only 2 parallel requests up to Summit $995/month ★★★★ Design Buffs B2B SaaS marketing teams SaaS specialism, dedicated PM 3-month minimum commitment $1,500/month ★★★★ Each service below has a screenshot, real pricing, and honest pros and cons. If the whole design-as-a-service model is new to you, that primer is a good starting point. We start with Awesomic, then work through the rest. Awesomic Best for: startups that need design, web, and video handled together. Awesomic is a design-and-creative subscription and vetted talent platform. You get your design, no-code, video, and creative work done for a fixed monthly fee, matched to a pre-vetted designer instead of relying on one solo operator or hiring freelancers yourself. The contrast with a single-designer service is capacity and scope. We match you with talent from the top 0.82% of applicants in up to 24 hours, and because we're a platform rather than one person, we can scale you up, swap a match that isn't right, and keep work moving without a single point of failure. Where DesignJoy centers on one designer's output, we cover branding , UI/UX, product and web design, Webflow and Framer builds, plus video and motion. More than 4,000 businesses have run 20,000+ projects with us, and we hold a 4.9 rating on Google and Trustpilot. Key features: Matching to a vetted designer in up to 24 hours, so work starts the day you brief it Design, no-code (Webflow, Framer, WordPress), and video under one subscription, not a single discipline A dedicated project manager on the 1-to-1 tier to coordinate multi-part work Unlimited revisions on every plan, so you refine until it's right A free re-match if your designer isn't the right fit, so you're never stuck Slack integration on paid plans for real-time briefs and feedback Pricing: the Graphic Pack starts at $1,490/month (or $1,190/month billed quarterly) for part-time talent and graphic design. The All-in-one plan is $2,995/month (or $2,396/month quarterly) and adds no-code, copywriting, and QA. An AI Designer plan is $200/month, and the 1-to-1 tier with full-time dedicated talent plus a PM is custom. Quarterly plans have a 3-month minimum; monthly plans have no commitment. Pros: fast 24-hour matching, vetted top-tier talent, no single point of failure, broad scope, clear public pricing. Cons: not the cheapest entry point, quarterly plans carry a 3-month minimum. How to start using Awesomic: Choose a plan on our pricing page based on whether you need graphics only or the full design-plus-no-code-plus-video mix. Fill in a short brief covering your brand, goals, and first task. Get matched with a vetted designer in up to 24 hours. Submit your first request and collaborate over Slack or the dashboard. Review the first draft, request revisions until it's right, and download the final files. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it swaps a single operator and one plan for a scalable platform, 24-hour matching, and design, web, and video in one place, without the solo-operator risk. Final verdict: if you want the flat-fee simplicity DesignJoy is known for but with a team behind it and room to scale, Awesomic is the strongest all-round pick here. Get started and get matched within a day. Design Pickle Design Pickle is a creative-as-a-service platform offering unlimited-request graphic design, motion, and illustration from a dedicated, brand-trained team, aimed at teams that want managed delivery at scale. Key features: A brand-trained dedicated team with a production coordinator and art director on tap First drafts back the next business day, with most requests done in 24–48 hours Unlimited revisions and broad file-format delivery with full client IP Pricing: custom and quote-only as of 2026, set on a consultation call, with quarterly or annual billing. There's no public rate to compare directly. Pros: dedicated brand-trained team, fast stated turnaround, full IP ownership. Cons: no public pricing without a sales call, quarterly or annual billing only, no month-to-month option. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it swaps one solo designer for a managed team with coordinators, which suits higher, steadier graphic volume. Final verdict: a strong managed option if you can accept quote-based pricing and don't need a public number to decide. Penji Penji is an unlimited graphic design subscription with a dedicated remote team and art-director oversight, built for SMBs and agencies that want a low, predictable entry price. Key features: Unlimited requests and revisions across 120+ design services 1-day delivery on the Business and Marketing tiers A white-label client portal on the Agency plan for reselling design work Pricing: Business is $499/month, Marketing & Ads is $995/month, and Agency is $1,995/month, with 15% off quarterly and 20% off yearly, plus a 30-day money-back guarantee. Pros: low entry price, broad scope, 30-day guarantee. Cons: only 1 project at a time on the $499 tier, motion and video gated to the $1,995 plan, no free trial. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it costs a fraction of DesignJoy's single plan, which makes it an easy first switch for graphics-led teams. Final verdict: the best-value entry point here if you can work within one active project at a time. Kimp Kimp is a flat-fee unlimited subscription that bundles graphic design and video under one plan, with a dedicated team, a project manager, and the KIMP360 platform. Key features: Separate Graphics, Video, and combined plans, so you pay for the work you need A dedicated team plus a project manager on every plan Unlimited team members can submit and manage requests at no extra cost Pricing: Graphics or Video is $1,397/month and Graphics + Video is $1,697/month; a promo currently halves the first four months, but plan around the list price. Enterprise plans are quote-based. Pros: graphics and video in one subscription, dedicated team, unlimited seats. Cons: throughput capped at 2–5 active requests, list price is steep, the advertised rate is a promo. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: where DesignJoy leans web and brand, Kimp adds video and motion in the same subscription. Final verdict: a strong pick for content teams that need graphics and short-form video together. ManyPixels ManyPixels is an unlimited graphic, web, and motion design subscription where you submit as many requests as you want to a chosen designer for a flat fee. Key features: Full copyright and IP transfer plus native source files on every delivery Next-business-day first drafts and a Slack channel with your designer Unlimited brands under one plan, handy for agencies Pricing: Advanced is $699/month ($559/month billed annually) and Business is $1,199/month ($959/month annually). You can pause for $10/month and keep file access. Pros: full IP and source files, choose your designer, pause option. Cons: no sub-$500 or free tier, base tier works the queue serially, confusing tier naming. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it delivers a comparable flat-fee model at a third of the price, with editable source files handed over. Final verdict: a dependable mid-priced option for teams that want to own their working files. Superside Superside is a subscription creative-as-a-service agency for mid-market and enterprise teams, with senior, AI-native squads across video, motion, branding, web, and presentations. Key features: Senior specialists across a wide creative range under one contract The Superspace platform with Brand Brain for on-brand AI-assisted briefing Flex plans roll over unused budget for up to three months Pricing: plans start at a $15,000/month minimum on a 12-month commitment, plus a $1,000/month software fee. Everything above the floor is custom. Pros: deep senior bench, wide scope, budget rollover on Flex. Cons: $15,000/month floor and mandatory annual term, extra software fee, no self-serve option. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it's the enterprise step up for teams whose volume dwarfs what one designer or one plan can handle. Final verdict: the right pick only for enterprises replacing an agency, not lean teams watching spend. Flocksy Flocksy is a flat-rate creative subscription sold in daily-hour blocks, giving you the same dedicated team (designer, video editor, motion editor, illustrator, plus copywriter support) across every brief. Key features: The same named team every project, so it learns your brand Unused hours roll over for up to 30 days Unlimited requests and revisions across 140+ services Pricing: plans run from $1,199/month for 2 daily hours up to $2,999/month for 6 daily hours (billed annually), with a Production Coordinator from the 4-hour tier and an Art Director from the 6-hour tier. Pros: consistent dedicated team, rollover hours, transparent time tracking. Cons: advertised prices need annual billing, entry tier has no coordinator, video gated to higher plans. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it keeps DesignJoy's single-team continuity but adds a multi-person team so nothing stalls on one person. Final verdict: a good fit for brands that want a steady team without the solo-operator risk. Delesign Delesign is an unlimited-request design subscription that pairs you with a dedicated senior designer and a design manager who work through your queue. Key features: A named senior designer (5+ years) plus a design manager A free designer swap if the fit isn't right A 15-day money-back guarantee that lets you keep completed designs Pricing: the graphic design plan is $599/month, with separate tracks for web development ($649/month), multimedia ($799/month), and SEO writing ($399/month). Pros: dedicated senior designer, keep the work after a refund, separate design and dev tracks. Cons: the queue runs about 2 hours per business day and is serial, no free trial, animation can take 7–15 days. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: it offers a named-designer relationship, like DesignJoy, at roughly an eighth of the monthly price. Final verdict: a solid mid-priced pick when a consistent designer matters more than parallel speed. Kapa99 Kapa99 is a flat-fee unlimited graphic design subscription that works your requests in parallel rather than one at a time, aimed at small businesses that want speed. Key features: Unlimited active tasks worked in parallel, not a single queue Native Adobe files plus Canva delivery on every plan A 15-day free trial with no card and a 30-day money-back guarantee Pricing: Async Standard is $499/month (2-day delivery), Async Priority is $999/month (1-day), and the Dedicated Team tier is $2,500/month (same-day), with a first-two-months intro discount. Pros: parallel task handling, free trial, month-to-month. Cons: output can be uneven, top tier is a big jump, no per-task option. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: its parallel-task model directly answers DesignJoy's one-request-at-a-time bottleneck, at a far lower entry price. Final verdict: worth trialing if throughput on a budget is your priority; use the free trial to test quality first. DotYeti DotYeti is a flat-rate unlimited graphic design subscription with a dedicated team and unusually clear, tier-based turnaround SLAs. Key features: Published day-based turnaround that tightens by tier Motion, video, 3D, and basic web development on higher tiers A 14-day satisfaction guarantee with no long-term contract Pricing: Base is $995/month, Scale is $1,595/month, Summit is $2,595/month, and Apex Studio starts at $3,995/month, with roughly 10% off on six-month prepay. Pros: transparent published SLAs, broad scope on higher tiers, no lock-in. Cons: only 2 requests run in parallel up through Summit, entry price is high, top tier is quote-heavy. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: its written SLAs give you predictable delivery dates, where a solo service depends on one person's schedule. Final verdict: a good match for teams that want delivery commitments in writing. Design Buffs Design Buffs is a subscription design agency built specifically for B2B SaaS and technology marketing teams, selling capacity in monthly hours with a dedicated project manager. Key features: A dedicated Creative Project Manager plus an assigned designer pool Unlimited requests and revisions within your monthly hours A specialism in B2B software and technology brands Pricing: Essential is $1,500/month (40 hours; $1,238/month billed annually) and Growth is $2,800/month (80 hours), with a Webflow development add-on at $999/month. A 3-month minimum applies. Pros: SaaS specialism, dedicated PM, quarterly and annual discounts. Cons: 3-month minimum commitment, Webflow is a paid add-on, no day-based SLA published. Why it's a good DesignJoy alternative: if you're a SaaS marketing team, its focus and dedicated PM fit better than a generalist solo designer. Final verdict: the specialist pick for B2B SaaS teams that value industry focus over the lowest price. Pros and cons of switching from DesignJoy Switching has clear upsides, but weigh the friction too. On the upside, you can trade a single point of failure for a team that keeps working if one person is out, run several projects in parallel instead of one at a time, and often pay far less than $4,995/month for a comparable flat-fee service. Many alternatives also offer a trial or month-to-month billing, so you can test before committing. If you're still weighing the model itself, our comparison of freelancers, in-house, or a subscription lays out the trade-offs. On the downside, a new team spends the first few weeks learning your brand, so expect a short dip while it ramps. You'll re-share brand assets, rebuild templates, and set a new feedback rhythm. And a lower price sometimes means tighter limits on active requests or narrower scope, so read the terms, not just the headline rate. The honest read: if DesignJoy's price, capacity ceiling, or solo-operator risk is a real problem for you, switching pays off. If you value one specific designer's hand and the price isn't a strain, staying may be simpler. How much do DesignJoy alternatives cost? DesignJoy's single plan sits at the high end of the flat-fee market, so most alternatives come in well below it. Here's the lowest public monthly entry point for each. Service Entry plan Starting price Billing note Penji Business $499/month 15% off quarterly, 20% yearly Kapa99 Async Standard $499/month Intro discount first 2 months Delesign Marketer Growth $599/month Month-to-month ManyPixels Advanced $699/month $559/month billed annually DotYeti Base $995/month ~10% off 6-month prepay Flocksy 2 Daily Hours $1,199/month Billed annually Kimp Graphics $1,397/month Promo halves first 4 months Awesomic Graphic Pack $1,490/month $1,190/month quarterly Design Buffs Essential $1,500/month 3-month minimum Design Pickle Custom Quote-only Quarterly or annual Superside Flex $15,000/month Annual term + software fee The gap is stark: several capable services start under $700/month, roughly a seventh of DesignJoy's rate. The trade-off is usually team size and parallel throughput, so read what each plan includes rather than anchoring on price alone. Our overview of monthly design services breaks down what each price tier typically buys. This tracks a broader hiring shift, too: The CMO Survey found the share of planned marketing hiring going to full-time staff fell from 82.5% in 2019 to 77.9% in 2025, with the rest moving toward independent and flexible talent. How hard is it to migrate from DesignJoy? Moving off DesignJoy is straightforward because there's no technical lock-in, just context to transfer. Plan for a few days of prep and one project cycle to settle in. Download your finished files and any source assets from your DesignJoy board before you cancel. Build a brand kit: logo files, fonts, color codes, tone notes, and two or three examples of work you liked. Pick your new service and start with a real but low-stakes task, so you can judge quality and turnaround safely. Set up your feedback channel (Slack, a dashboard, or a board) and agree on how revisions get flagged. Run one full cycle, note where drafts missed, and tighten the brief for the next round. Because DesignJoy already works through a Trello board, exporting your history and reference links is quick. Expect the new team's first week or two to run slightly slower while it learns your brand, then you'll be back to full speed with the capacity and pricing gaps closed. Common mistakes to avoid when choosing an alternative A few errors trip up teams switching from a solo service to a team-based one: Assuming every "alternative" is a real business. Some sites ranking as DesignJoy alternatives are template clones with no track record, so check for a client list, dated case studies, and a team page before you trust a ranking. Chasing the lowest price and ignoring throughput. A cheap plan with one active request can be slower than a pricier one running several. Forgetting to check who does the work. A named designer, a rotating pool, and a solo operator carry very different risks. Skipping the trial. Onboarding quality shows in the first project, so test with a real task first. Overlooking scope. If you need video, motion, or web alongside design, confirm it's included rather than a second vendor. Avoiding these comes down to matching the service to your real workload and verifying the provider is legitimate. Write down your must-haves, then trial the two closest fits before you cancel. How to choose the right DesignJoy alternative for your needs The best pick depends on why DesignJoy stopped fitting. A simple way to decide: If you want DesignJoy's flat-fee simplicity but with a team behind it and room to scale, Awesomic fits, since 24-hour matching and a platform model remove the single-person ceiling. If your issue is mainly price, Penji, Kapa99, or Delesign start under $700/month. If you need several projects running at once, Kapa99's parallel model or a multi-person team like Flocksy answers that directly. If you need bundled video, Kimp is built for it, and if you're a B2B SaaS team, Design Buffs brings industry focus. Enterprises with serious volume should look at Superside. It also helps to compare the wider field in an independent design subscription directory before you commit. And if you're weighing specific tools, we've also compared Design Pickle alternatives , Kimp alternatives , and Superside competitors in their own guides. Whatever you shortlist, trial two before committing. The right DesignJoy alternative is the one that fixes your specific gap, whether that's price, parallel throughput, or removing single-person risk. Our roundup of design service models can help you weigh the options side by side. The bottom line on switching DesignJoy's premium single plan and solo-operator model are exactly what push growing teams to look around. The real win from switching isn't just a lower bill, it's removing the capacity ceiling and single point of failure while keeping the flat-fee simplicity you liked. Decide what matters most, whether that's parallel work, a named team, or bundled video, then trial your top two with a real task and keep the one whose first drafts land closest to your brand. Do that and you'll trade one person's schedule for a service that scales with you. FAQs What is the best DesignJoy alternative in 2026? It depends on your priority. For flat-fee simplicity with a team behind it and room to scale, Awesomic is the strongest all-round pick. For a lower price, Penji and Kapa99 start at $499/month, and for parallel throughput, Kapa99's model or a multi-person team like Flocksy fits best. Why is DesignJoy so expensive? DesignJoy charges $4,995/month for a single plan because it's positioned as senior, one-designer output with fast turnaround and a limited client roster. Many alternatives deliver comparable flat-fee design with a team for well under $700/month, though usually with a different quality and continuity profile. Is DesignJoy really run by one person? Yes. In a public Reddit AMA, DesignJoy's founder confirmed the service runs through him personally, which is why alternatives with a full team appeal to buyers who want redundancy and the ability to run several projects at once. Are DesignJoy alternatives cheaper? Almost always. Several capable services start between $499 and $999 per month, a fraction of DesignJoy's $4,995 plan. The trade-off is usually a team-based model versus one senior designer, so compare scope and throughput, not just the price. Can I run multiple projects at once with these alternatives? Some are built for it. Kapa99 works unlimited tasks in parallel, and team-based services like Awesomic, Kimp, and Flocksy handle several projects at once, unlike DesignJoy's one-request-at-a-time queue.

title: Introducing API Version 2025-12-01
summary: We're excited to announce the release of API version 2025-12-01 — introducing inbound funding workflows with Payment Instruments.
body_text: We’re excited to announce the release of API version 2025-12-01 , featuring the new Payment Instruments API for inbound funding workflows. This version enables liability accounts to receive direct payments via ACH or wire transfer — allowing third parties to send funds directly to liability accounts without requiring explicit Payment creation. ​ What’s New ​ Payment Instruments API Method now supports inbound funding workflows with the introduction of a new PaymentInstrument type: inbound_achwire_payment . This feature allows liability accounts (e.g., loans, credit cards) to receive direct payments via ACH or wire transfer. Key features: Provisions a unique virtual account number and routing number linked to a specific Method Account, effectively making the underlying liability routable Third parties can send funds directly to these credentials, and Method automatically applies the funds to the associated account, without requiring you to explicitly create a Payment Supports use cases such as payroll, refinancing, and other direct payment scenarios How it works: Create Instrument : Create a Payment Instrument of type inbound_achwire_payment for a specific Method Account Receive Banking Details : Method returns unique account_number and routing_number Share with a Third Party : Provide these banking details to a third party (e.g., payroll provider, refinance lender, or another bank) Inbound Transfer : When funds are sent to these credentials, Method receives the inbound ACH or wire transfer Automatic Application : Method automatically applies the received funds to the associated account Available when passing Method-Version: 2025-12-01 in the request header. Example Request curl https://production.methodfi.com/accounts/acc_4m9amk4KFiaQX/payment_instruments \ -X POST \ -H "Method-Version: 2025-12-01" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_WyZEWVfTcH7GqmPzUPk65Vjc" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "type": "inbound_achwire_payment" }' Example Response { "id" : "pmt_inst_cLbaArHhfDBDf" , "account_id" : "acc_GAzrD99cUqGEN" , "type" : "inbound_achwire_payment" , "card" : null , "network_token" : null , "inbound_achwire_payment" : { "account_number" : "2517228863" , "routing_number" : "026015244" }, "chargeable" : true , "status" : "completed" , "error" : null , "created_at" : "2025-12-11T00:12:58.639Z" , "updated_at" : "2025-12-11T00:12:58.639Z" } See Payment Instruments for more information. ​ Simulate API The Simulate API now supports simulating inbound ACH / wire payments for inbound_achwire_payment Payment Instruments — making it easier for developers to test inbound payment flows in the development environment. Simulate Inbound ACH/Wire Payments This endpoint allows developers to simulate receiving an inbound payment and triggers the same automatic payment application logic used in production. Available when passing Method-Version: 2025-12-01 in the request header. This API is available in the development environment only. For more information, visit the Simulations API documentation. ​ Breaking Changes Payment Instrument product names changed The payment_instrument product name has been split into three separate product names: payment_instrument.card payment_instrument.network_token payment_instrument.inbound_achwire_payment In previous versions ( 2024-04-04 , 2025-07-04 ), the Account object’s products , restricted_products , subscriptions , available_subscriptions , and restricted_subscriptions arrays contained the single product name payment_instrument . In 2025-12-01 , these arrays now contain the three separate product names instead of the single payment_instrument name. ​ Why It Matters This release enables new inbound funding workflows that simplify payment collection for liability accounts. By introducing inbound_achwire_payment Payment Instruments, developers can now: Enable third parties to send payments directly to liability accounts without explicit Payment creation Streamline payroll, refinancing, and other direct payment scenarios Automatically apply inbound transfers to the associated account Test inbound payment flows more easily with enhanced Simulate API support ​ Upgrading to 2025-12-01 The new API version is available to all existing teams. New teams are automatically pinned to 2025-12-01 . Request Header: Set Method-Version to 2025-12-01 . See API Versioning for more information Client Libraries: method-node and method-python v2.1.0+ default to this version Once upgraded, rollbacks to prior API versions are not supported. Contact your Method CSM for upgrade assistance. ​ Upgrade Support Our technical integration team is available to guide you through the migration. Contact your Method CSM to schedule a review of your current payment integration or to receive a personalized upgrade checklist.

title: New Seam Java SDK
summary: This week we are excited to the beta launch of our Java SDK.
body_text: This week we are excited to the beta launch of our Java SDK. You can now use Seam inside your Java applications. You can browse the entire SDK repo here . Why Release a Java SDKs? ☕ At Seam, we aim to provide the best developer experience to control IoT devices. Part of that effort consists of producing great SDKs that make Seam even easier to use, and IoT devices even simpler to control. We design these SDKs to match the programming environment in which Seam is being used. We also strongly encourage developers to use the Seam SDK in their preferred language versus using the Seam HTTP API directly. Many Java developers already use Seam to control IoT devices. Unfortunately, until today, we did not have a proper Java SDK for them. We are now trying to make up for this grave injavastice 😊 Getting Started with the Seam Java SDK You can use either Gradle or Maven to pull in the Seam Java SDK into your project. As with other Seam SDK, you then just need to provide your API key to begin using it, such as in the example below. 1 SeamApiClient seam = SeamApiClient . builder ( ) 2 . token ( "MY_API_KEY" ) 3 . build ( ) ; 4 AccessCodesCreateResponse accessCodesCreateResponse = 5 seam . accessCodes ( ) . create ( AccessCodesCreateRequest . builder ( ) 6 . deviceId ( "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000" ) 7 . commonCodeKey ( "My first code" ) 8 . build ( ) ) ; 9 System . out . println ( accessCodesCreateResponse . getAccessCode ( ) ) ; This Java SDK is still in beta but we will be rapidly iterating toward a stable version. If you find issues, please leave us a note at support@getseam.com .
